notes: Account summary: mid-size adtech platform using chat for creative assist + reranking for personalized feed. Very sensitive to tail latency during peak campaign launches.
Primary ask: committed throughput guarantee for Dedicated pool with predictable unit cost. Wants billing alignment to sustained tokens/sec, not just reserved GPUs.

Throughput targets requested by client: min sustained 60,000 tokens/sec across the reserved pool during business hours (08:00-20:00 PT), with 1,200 concurrent chat sessions cap. P95 latency target: <= 150ms for <512-token responses; P50 ~40ms.

Burst policy: allow 30s bursts up to 250,000 tokens/sec for campaign spikes, capped to 3x per hour and subject to burst-instance availability. Client insists burst not billed at full committed rate — negotiating tiered burst billing (50% of committed rate for first 2 bursts/hr, full rate thereafter).

Reserved GPU planning: initial ask for 8xA100-80GB persistent nodes for baseline, plus 2x burst nodes (preemptible style) that can be spun up within 90s. Discussed alternate config with 16xA10G to lower cost but client worried about quantization/quality differences.

Routing & fallback: require automatic fallback to smaller model variant when burst capacity exhausted; fallbacks must preserve >85% metric on reranking NDCG (client-provided eval set). Also require cross-region failover to us-east as backup for NA outages.

SLA negotiation points: credit structure proposed — 5% credit for monthly availability <99.5%, additional credit if throughput floor missed >2% of measured minutes in a month. Client pushing for tighter thresholds; legal concern over indemnity language.

POC notes: SE tuned batching/kv-cache and improved sustained tokens/sec by ~22% on short-context tests. Longer-context generation still 8-12% below client’s expected sustained rate — plan to try alternative kernel/quantization and confirm in next POC iteration.
Quote from Aperture eng lead: 'We need predictable tail performance when campaigns spike — inconsistent bursts kill CTR.'
Commercial ask: minimum 12-month reserved commitment, optional annual true-up. Budget owner wants step-down clause after quarter 2 if actual token usage < 60% of commitment.

Open items: finalize burst billing model, add explicit measurement methodology for tokens/sec (sampling windows and monitoring tags), legal to accept Redwood outage credit formula or propose counter-offer.
